spec.description: The function receives a `craftRequest` object containing a numeric `recipeId`, an `inventory` array, and an optional `recipes` array. If `recipes` is not supplied, a built-in global recipe list is used. It locates the recipe with the matching `id` in the chosen list; if none exists, it returns `success: false`, the original `inventory` unchanged, and the error `'Unknown recipe'`. Otherwise, it deep‑clones the input `inventory` and works on the copy. For each ingredient in the recipe, it scans the copy’s slots sequentially, decrementing counts of matching‑`itemId` entries and setting a slot to `null` when its count reaches zero. If any ingredient cannot be fully satisfied, it returns `success: false`, the **original** (unmutated) `inventory`, and an error string indicating the missing ingredient item ID and required quantity. When all ingredients are consumed, it adds the recipe’s result items to the clone: first it tops off any existing slots that hold the result item, respecting a per‑item maximum stack size taken from the `ITEMS` definition (with a fallback default when no definition is present); then it fills empty slots (`null` or zero‑count) with new stacks of the result, splitting into multiple stacks if the output quantity exceeds the maximum stack size. If inventory space is insufficient to hold the full result, no error is signalled—the result added is silently capped by available capacity. Finally, it returns `success: true`, the modified inventory copy, and an empty error string. The operation is deterministic, does not mutate the input `inventory`, and has no side effects beyond return values.
